The work merged.
Clear the worktree.

Ten worktrees. Seven merged last week.
And a folder full of handoffs nobody reads.

Lumberjack proves what landed, removes those worktrees on its own, and keeps every branch. Finished work documents wait in a trash before they go; research and unfinished work stay.

        BEFORE INSTALLWHAT THE SWEEP PRINTS

        The example simulates a repository; nothing on your machine is read. Squash or rebase merge? The sweep proves it from git when the merged content matches, or from the exact tip of a merged PR with a logged-in gh. Patch similarity alone never removes anything.

        02 / LEAVE IT ON

        Automatic. Careful.
        Undoable.

        Lumberjack is built to run unattended in a repository full of agent work. It acts only on proof, keeps anything that could still matter, and leaves a way back.

        • RUNS ITSELF

          No command to remember.

          The sweep runs at every session start in Claude Code and Codex, and after each merge through a git post-merge hook.

          session start  → sweep
git merge      → sweep

        • PROVES IT LANDED

          Merged means merged.

          A worktree goes only when its tip is in origin/main, its content already is (squash merges), or a merged pull request had exactly that tip. Similar-looking patches never count.

        • NEVER LOSES WORK

          Eight reasons to stay.

          Uncommitted files, unpushed commits, a locked or brand-new worktree, evidence, or untracked docs keep a worktree in place. The sweep names the reason.

          blocked claude/eng-203-search: dirty

        • UNDO ANYTHING

          Branches stay. Docs wait in a trash.

          Removing a worktree deletes no commits; one command brings it back. Work documents move to a trash inside .git/ and stay there for 30 days before the purge.

          git worktree add ../app-eng-205 claude/eng-205-ui

        • SEE IT FIRST

          Preview, or only report.

          --preview prints what the next session start would remove, trash and purge, with file counts, and changes nothing. cleanup = "report" keeps it that way; --tally shows what was done.

        • YOURS TO TUNE

          One small TOML file.

          Setup reads the repository, asks a few questions with recommended answers, and writes .lumberjack.toml. It never commits; you review the diff.

          cleanup = "prune"
doc_roots = ["docs/work"]
[doc_strategy]
scope = "bundle"
grace_days = 7
trash_days = 30

        Also included: agents keep to your branch names and work in worktrees. If one tries to finish its turn on a branch named outside your pattern, or after switching the main checkout away from main, it is stopped once with the fix. stop_gate = false turns this off.

        INSTALL

        Put it to work.

        Install for your agent, run setup in the repository, then review and commit the changes. The next session start runs the sweep.

        REQUIREMENTS

        Git + Python 3.11 or newer.
        gh is optional, for pull-request evidence.

        Full installation guide ↗
        IN CLAUDE CODE, ONE AT A TIME
        1. /plugin marketplace add VforVal/lumberjack
        2. /plugin install lumberjack@lumberjack
        THEN, IN YOUR REPOSITORY

        Restart Claude Code, then run:

        /lumberjack:setup

        Answer the setup questions. Review git diff and commit the generated configuration.

        IN YOUR TERMINAL
        1. codex plugin marketplace add VforVal/lumberjack
        2. codex plugin add lumberjack@lumberjack
        THEN, IN CODEX

        Restart Codex. Run /hooks once to review and trust the plugin hooks, then choose lumberjack:setup from the skill picker. Review git diff and commit.

        Updating? Re-run setup after each plugin update, so it can ask about new settings. Standard-library Python; no runtime packages to install.

        Before enabling cleanup, see the plan with sweep_worktrees.py --preview.
